question: The province view's building columns (buildings_left / buildings_right, CBuildingMember: which buildings, its update and enabling, the ten pips, its tooltip, its right click) and its underground window to its end (the gate 0x6EA920, the bar, the suppression text, which mouse button steps underground_mission which way).

addresses.name: CBuildingMember::CBuildingMember
addresses.signature: CBuildingMember* __stdcall CBuildingMember::CBuildingMember(CBuildingMember* this, CBuilding* building, void* usedShortcuts) @EAX
addresses.comment: **One building's row in the province view** (window `building_member`, province_interface.gui), 0xA0 bytes (the refresh's operator new). `ret 0xC`; `this` on the stack. Makes the window through the in-game screen's gui (+0x20), writes vftable 0x15D3E38 / 0x15D3E6C (+0x1C), building -> +0x28, +0x2C (province) = 0, and binds `building_icon`'s observer glue (+0x50, VCBuildingMember::__CButtonObserverGlue, 0x50 bytes; constructor 0x6EAF10): its slot 2 (plain click) = CBuildingMember::OnClick (0x6DBE40), its slot 9 (right click) = CBuildingMember::OnRightClick (0x6DBB00). **The label and the keyboard shortcut**: walks the building's name (CBuilding slot 6, the localised text at +0x38) character by character against `usedShortcuts` (a list of characters shared by every row the refresh makes, left column first); the first character not on it is added to it and becomes the button's shortcut (button slot 55, from a one-character string), and +0x30 becomes the name with that character wrapped in \xA7Y ... \xA7W; with every character taken, +0x30 is the plain name and the shortcut string empty. Byte compare, so case counts: in Their Finest Hour the keys come out A, N, C, L, n (Anti-Aircraft Guns), R, u (Nuclear Reactor), o (Rocket Test Site), I, f (Infrastructure). The button's sprite is set to `GFX_provinceview_` + the building's key (+0x1C) through its slot 57.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole to the `ret 0xC` at 0x6DBAF6: the push of 0x6DBE40 as the glue constructor's first argument and 0x6DBB00 as its fifteenth (0x6DB6C5-0x6DB6E5) land at glue +8 and +0x40 by 0x6EAF10's stores, and the glue vftable 0x15D3ECC's slot 2 (0x62D620) calls +8 with no argument and slot 9 (0x6C35C0) calls +0x40 with one; the loop at 0x6DB74A-0x6DB7ED with the list walk `cmp byte [eax], cl` and the \xA7Y/\xA7W strings 0x15B5C54/0x15B6700; slot 0xDC on `building_icon` with the one-character string; `GFX_provinceview_` at 0x6DB6F5 plus +0x1C. Two callers, both in the refresh (0x6DE824, 0x6DE8E1), each pushing the same list [esp+0x5C]. Shown wrong if slot 55 is not the shortcut setter (TButton::ClearShortcut's record calls it the refill from a string) or slot 57 not the sprite setter.

addresses.name: CBuildingMember::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 8: a building row's enabling and its ten pips**, run for every row by the view's update (0x6E7C00). **Enabling** (button slot 46 enable / 47 disable): in a custom game's setup where 0x4208B0 answers true, disabled. Otherwise, with more than one object selected, enabled where any selected province (selectable kind 3) controlled by the player passes CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed (IsBuildingAllowedIgnoringLevel in a custom game's setup); with one or none, enabled where the row's province (+0x2C) is controlled by the player and passes it. **Pips** `plupp_0`..`plupp_N-1`, N = the building's max_level (+0x68), sprite GFX_prov_building_plupp (3 frames: 1 green, 2 orange, 3 grey). intel = the player's intelligence of the province (+0x370[player], 0 past +0x374). Where intel >= 6, or the building's modifier is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE (12) and intel >= 1: built = trunc(level_max / 1000.0), working = level_current / 1000.0 (single precision), queued = the sizes (+0x40) of the **player's** building lines (+0xF40, slot 16) of this building located here; pip i (1-based) hidden where i > built + queued, else shown with frame 3 where i > built, frame 2 where i > working, frame 1 otherwise. Else, for infrastructure (intel 0) with MaxInfrastructure (+0x5C) below floor(200.5) = 200: every pip hidden. Else: pip 1 given frame 1 (slot 18, **not shown**) where level_max / 1000.0 > 0 and hidden otherwise; pips 2..N hidden. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: vtable.py --holding 0x6DC380: CBuildingMember slot 8 only. Disassembled whole, 0x6DC380 to the bare `ret`s at 0x6DC834, 0x6DC958 and 0x6DCB1A (the next function, the destructor, is slot 0 at 0x6DCB20). The intel `cmp esi,6; jge` at 0x6DC71F, the modifier test `cmp [ecx+0x24],0xc` at 0x6DC731/0x6DC742, the global [0x1A8A6F0] written once by the static initialiser at 0xCDB480 from floor(200.5f); the frame choice at 0x6DCAB5-0x6DCAF0 (push 3 / 2 / 1). Frame colours measured on gfx/interface/prov_building_plupp.dds (48x16, three 16-pixel frames: mean (109,202,86), (154,75,22), (144,144,144)). Slot 13 = show, 14 = hide, 18 = set frame from their use here and in the record's other buttons; shown wrong if slot 13 were not Show, which would change only the low-intel pip remark.

addresses.name: CBuildingMember::OnRightClick
addresses.comment: **A right click on a building row** (the glue's slot 9). Outside a custom game's setup it returns at once: **a right click does nothing in a game**. In the setup: for every selected province (kind 3) controlled by the player whose built level (level_max / 1000) is above 0, new = level - 1, refused below the province's default level (0x41B700) unless the settings' +0x78 flag for the building is set, refused at 0 for an air base with aircraft based (province +0x304 built and +0x54's +0xC above 0), a naval base with ships (+0x300, +0x58) or infrastructure with province +0x2C0 above 0 (read from the shape, not followed); else posts CCgmSetBuildingLevelCommand(building, province id, new). `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole to the `ret 4` at 0x6DBE32: the test of GetCustomGameSettings' first byte at 0x6DBB21-0x6DBB2A jumps straight to the exit; the command built at 0x6DBD6D (0x42CAD0, 0x48 bytes) with the level less one. The right click: glue +0x40, called by the glue vftable's slot 9 (0x6C35C0), and slot 9 is the right click by the maintainer's word on another glue of the same interface (FINDINGS-leaderwindow.md section 6); the custom game's CGM_TOOLTIP_BUILDING_SHORTCUT ("RMB to decrease the level") agrees. Shown wrong if slot 9 were another event.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_BuildBuildingTooltip
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ProvinceView_BuildBuildingTooltip(void* view, GuiTooltipText* out, Hoi3CString* listName, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: **The tooltip of a building row's button or pip**, asked by BuildProvinceViewTooltip for `building_icon` and `plupp_0`..`plupp_9`, once with `buildings_left` and once with `buildings_right`. Walks that list box's rows for the one whose window holds the element (TListboxItem slot 22). With the player's intelligence of the view's province (+0x24) below 6: `text` = the building's name (CProvinceBuilding slot 7 -> CBuilding slot 6) and nothing else. Otherwise, **`building_icon`**: `text` = the row's +0x30 (the name with its shortcut letter in yellow); then into `delayed`: the building not available to the player's technology -> PV_NB_TECH and, where the building has an unlocking technology (+0x10), "\n (\xA7R*) " + its name; else in a custom game's setup with the player controlling the province -> 0x6E3D90's text, and CGM_TOOLTIP_BUILDING_SHORTCUT into `delayed_extra`; else the province not controlled by the player -> PV_NB_HOSTILE_TERR; else whole built levels plus the **player's** queued lines here at or above max_level -> PV_NB_MAX_SIZE; else, **where the province has a CPort (+0x354) and the building is port = yes**, PV_BUILD_ONLY_IN_PORT; else nothing. **A pip**: appended to `text`: level_max 0 -> PV_BUILD_NO_YET; level_current equal to level_max -> PV_BUILD_W_DESC with MAX = level_max to no places; else PV_BUILD_DESC with CURR = level_current to three places and MAX = level_max to none (FormatFloat, rounded); then, where the **province controller's** building lines of this building here have any size, "\n" + PV_CURR_CONS_MORE. Neither part ever states a cost or a time. `ret 0x10`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole: three exits, `ret 0x10` at 0x6E9A84, 0x6E9EA9 and 0x6E9FFE, with int3 after the last; the arguments read at [ebp+8] (view: +0x20, +0x24), [ebp+0xC] (out: +0, +0x1C, +0x38 are written), [ebp+0x10] (passed to the gui's list-box lookup), [ebp+0x14] (the element). The two calls at BuildProvinceViewTooltip with the strings buildings_left / buildings_right. The port test at 0x6E9F3F (`cmp [ecx+0x354],0; je exit`, then `cmp byte [edx+0x61],0; je exit`) - the text is shown only where a CPort exists. The queue owner: [esp+0x6C] is the player's country for the button (0x6E927B) and the province controller's for the pips (0x6E9349-0x6E935F). Keys checked in both installs' localisation.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_GetUndergroundProvince
addresses.comment: **Which province the view's `underground` window is about, or none (the window hidden).** With fewer than two objects selected: in a custom game's setup the view's province (+0x24) where Underground_CanPlaceIn(it, player, false); otherwise the view's province where its underground's level_max is above 0 and either its underground_owner is the player or Underground_CanPlaceIn(it, player, false), i.e. the player could have an underground there. With two or more: the **first selected province** (selection order, kind 3) passing the same test (the custom-game arm inlines CanPlaceIn's checks); none, null. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole: `ret 4` at 0x6EAB77, 0x6EAB8D, 0x6EABDE and 0x6EAC46; the selection count test `cmp [eax+0x130C],1; jle` at 0x6EAA4E; the level test `cmp [edx+0x20],0; jle` at 0x6EAB19; the owner test against the player id (+0xC34) at 0x6EAB25; Underground_CanPlaceIn with `push 0` at 0x6EAB46 and 0x6EABBC. One caller, the view's update at 0x6E8860, which hides the window (the window's +0x18 slot 14) where it answers null.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_OnUndergroundMissionLeftClick
addresses.comment: **A left click on `underground_mission` steps it forward**: frame (slot 19) 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 (anything below 3 goes up one, 3 and above to 1), the button set to it (slot 18), then ProvinceView_PostUndergroundMission(view, frame), which posts action frame - 1. So partisans -> spread -> none -> partisans. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, bare `ret` at 0x6EA483. Bound at the view constructor 0x6DDB1B as the +8 handler of the glue at view +0x148, which 0x6E3A93 attaches to `underground_mission`; that glue's vftable 0x15D3E0C has slot 2 (0x7478F0) calling +8 and slot 9 (0x6D0F30) calling +0x24. Slot 2 is the plain left click on the leader window's glues (FINDINGS-leaderwindow.md section 6, the maintainer confirming slot 9 the right click). Shown wrong if slot 2 were not the left click.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_OnUndergroundMissionRightClick
addresses.comment: **A right click on `underground_mission` steps it back**: frame below 2 -> 3, else frame - 1 (3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3), set, then ProvinceView_PostUndergroundMission(view, frame). So partisans -> none -> spread -> partisans. `ret 4`: the glue's slot 9 hands it an argument it never reads.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, `ret 4` at 0x6EA593 (0x6EA5A0 follows after int3). Stored at view +0x16C by the constructor (0x6DDB49), the glue +0x24 its vftable's slot 9 (0x6D0F30, `mov eax,[ecx+0x24]` with a stack argument) calls. Slot 9 is the right click by the maintainer's confirmation on the leader window (FINDINGS-leaderwindow.md section 6).

addresses.name: ProvinceView_CanMobilizeSelection
addresses.comment: Whether `spawn_partisan` is enabled. With two or more selected: any selected province with an underground (level_max > 0) owned by the player for which CanMobilizePartisans(player, it); otherwise CanMobilizePartisans(player, province) - the province being the one ProvinceView_GetUndergroundProvince chose. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and its exits read: `ret 4` at 0x6EAD74, 0x6EAD8A and 0x6EADA8; its province read from [ebp+8]. One caller, the view's update at 0x6E8956, which enables spawn_partisan (slot 46) on true outside a custom game's setup and disables it (slot 47) otherwise.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_CanSpreadSelection
addresses.comment: Whether `spawn_underground` is enabled: ProvinceView_CanMobilizeSelection with CanSpawnUnderground in place of CanMobilizePartisans. `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the same shape as 0x6EAC50 with CanSpawnUnderground; `ret 4` at 0x6EAED4, 0x6EAEEA and 0x6EAF08. One caller, the view's update at 0x6E8988.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_OnSpawnPartisanClick
addresses.comment: The left click of `spawn_partisan`: ProvinceView_OnSpawnButton(view, 0x786). Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: The whole body is push ecx; push 0x786; push ecx; call 0x6E1590; pop ecx; ret. Stored at view +0xF8 (0x6DDA8F), the +8 handler of the glue at +0xF0 that 0x6E395D attaches to `spawn_partisan`.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_OnSpawnUndergroundClick
addresses.comment: The left click of `spawn_underground`: ProvinceView_OnSpawnButton(view, 0x787). Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: The whole body is push ecx; push 0x787; push ecx; call 0x6E1590; pop ecx; ret. Stored at view +0x124 (0x6DDAD5), the +8 handler of the glue at +0x11C that 0x6E39F8 attaches to `spawn_underground`.

addresses.name: ProvinceView_OnCgmUndergroundBuild
addresses.comment: The custom-game setup's `cgm_underground_build` button (made in code at 0x6E3BEB, kept at view +0x174; labelled BUILD or DESTROY by the view's update). Outside the setup, nothing. In it: for each selected province (or the view's), with no underground and Underground_CanPlaceIn(player, false) and the setup's points (+0x24) covering the underground's price, CCgmSetUndergroundCommand(province, 1) and the points charged; with the player's own underground and the setup's +0x78 flag for the building, CCgmSetUndergroundCommand(province, 0) and the points refunded. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled only; bare `ret` at 0x6DE138 and 0x6DE332. Stored at view +0x180, the +8 handler of the glue at +0x178. The points arithmetic (0x41B370 / 1000) was not followed; custom-game only.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The row's `building_member` window, made by the constructor through the in-game screen's gui; every element is found through it.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov [esi+0x20],eax` from the gui's slot 11 with 'building_member'; Update and OnClick look up `building_icon` and `plupp_%d` through [this+0x20].

struct_fields.name: province
struct_fields.comment: The province the view shows, written into every row by the view's refresh (0x6DE953, 0x6DE973) each time it runs; 0 from the constructor. Update's single-selection enabling and its pips read it.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `mov [esi+0x2c],ebx` (0); the refresh's two walks store the view's +0x24 into each row's +0x2C; Update reads +0x338, +0x370/+0x374, +0x310, +0x5C through it.

struct_fields.name: label
struct_fields.comment: The building's name with its shortcut letter wrapped in \xA7Y ... \xA7W - the text of the button's tooltip. Built once by the constructor.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor: std::string at [esi+0x30] (capacity 0xF at +0x44) appended character by character at 0x6DB7C8 / 0x6DB8C7 / 0x6DB8EC; ProvinceView_BuildBuildingTooltip copies member+0x30 into the tooltip's text at 0x6E9A90.

struct_fields.name: click_observer
struct_fields.comment: A VCBuildingMember::__CButtonObserverGlue (vftable 0x15D3ECC, 0x50 bytes) attached to `building_icon`: owner at its +4, the plain click (slot 2, +8) CBuildingMember::OnClick, the right click (slot 9, +0x40) CBuildingMember::OnRightClick. Typed as a pointer for want of the glue's struct; it is embedded.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `lea eax,[esi+0x50]` as the glue constructor 0x6EAF10's receiver, then `building_icon`'s observer list (+0x48) slot 1 given [esi+0x50]; 0x6EAF10 writes 0x15D3ECC at +0 and stores through +0x4C.

struct_fields.name: unlocking_technology
struct_fields.comment: The technology that unlocks the building: its slot 7 gives the name the province view puts after PV_NB_TECH, and the production screen after NEED. Null where none does. Who fills it was not read.
struct_fields.evidence: ProvinceView_BuildBuildingTooltip at 0x6E9C48-0x6E9C61: `mov ecx,[building+0x10]; test; je`, then that object's slot 7 into a string appended to the tooltip; FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md section 2 reads the same field the same way. Inferred as to what writes it.
